Read correctly, M (u <= 2022) = +13.935m USD. The literal reading (-0.185m) is wrong: it needs UW2021 to have been 66,053 at end-2023 when the 2023 report printed 44,451, and UW2023 at 43,731 when the 2023 report printed 66,700.
1609_2024.note: The decisive evidence is the cell-by-cell overlay with the 2023 report, whose orientation is correct (columns = UW years, rows = ages; its by-year outstanding ties: 44,451-7,525=36,926, 108,475-9,650=98,825, 66,700-41=66,659). Reserve, paid and incurred totals are the same under either orientation, so they show the table is valid but do not fix the orientation. The uniform ~1% shift fits the stated consistent-rate retranslation. The wording 'pure underwriting year' and 'represented' says nothing of a reallocation.

4444_2017.explanation: No stated restatement of the claims history. Searched the 2017 report for restat / re-present / reclass / prior period / correction / change in accounting: only p21 'Previously, overseas deposits were included in the Statement of Cashflows ... The 2016 comparatives have also been prepared using this presentational basis' (cash flow presentation, not claims). The 2016 report's 'restated' items (p16, p28, p29, p31) are 2015 comparatives of investments and Lloyd's reporting, not claims. 2017 p25 says only: 'The tables below are presented at the exchange rates prevailing at 31 December 2017. ... Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred.' (same table wording as 2016 p24 apart from the deterioration sentence). p5 strategic report: 'A strengthening of prior period reserves'. Note 24 p42 gross claims: 'At 1 January 1,200,561; Increase/ (decrease) in provision 379,802; Foreign exchange (70,340); Other 37,196; At 31 December 1,547,219' (2016: 912,779; 166,053; 121,533; 196). The 'Other 37,196' (no reinsurers' share) is not explained anywhere in the filing.
4444_2017.transaction: p5: 'With effect from the 2016 year of account, CMA merged Syndicate 958's capacity into Syndicate 4444. The 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 will be reinsured to close into Syndicate 4444, effective from 1 January 2018.' p7: 'At 31 December 2017, Syndicate 4444 accepted the reinsurance to close for the 2015 year of account of Syndicate 958, its final underwriting year.' Effective date 1 Jan 2018 supports 'not in the 2017 figures', but the contract was accepted on 31 Dec 2017 and note 3d p19 says an accepted RITC's 'premium ... is recognised as income in the financial year that the RITC contract is signed, together with related claims liabilities'. I found no RITC premium or claims line in the 2017 accounts, so I cannot confirm or exclude that the unexplained 'Other 37,196' is connected. Not decisive for the base comparison (a 2018 effective RITC would not alter the end-2016 diagonal).

4444_2017.reconciliation_of_2016_base_to_2017_acco: No. Latest 2017 cells less the 2016 printed base give 1,112.6m (+10.3%) or 1,169.3m (+15.9% with 2010&prior) against gross incurred of 1,008.5m, and the gap widens once the base is retranslated to end-2017 rates. The 2017 table's own base is the closer fit (+6.3%), but it is itself 40.7m above the 2016 printed cells and neither passes the 5% criterion.
4444_2017.verdict_detail: The 2017 table's end-2016 history is not the 2016 report's history and the change is not explained. Individual cells move by up to +4.7% (older years) and -22.5% (2015 at age 0), outside the range sterling retranslation can produce (+3.5% to -8.1% per the p36 rates) and opposite in sign to the dominant US-dollar effect, and the ratio rises smoothly with age rather than being constant per currency mix. The filing states no restatement, correction or change of basis. The incurred test misses 5% (+6.3% against a -1.1% control), the paid proxy is +30.8% (control -6.2%; mixed-base because the 2017 table prints no end-2016 payments), and the claims reconciliation carries an unexplained 'Other 37,196'. The Syndicate 958 RITC is effective 1 Jan 2018 (p5), so it is unlikely to be in the end-2016 cells, but acceptance on 31 Dec 2017 (p7) and the unexplained 'Other' leave a small unresolved doubt. The movement is not measurable from the table with confidence: M is +118.2m on the 2017 table's own cells and +167.7m on the 2016 printed base (u 2011-2015), a 29% spread, and the filing prints no gross mature-cohort movement. 'Valid' (stated adverse development) is right about the sign (p25: 'in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred') but not about the base.
4444_2017.note: Why not valid: criteria need the table to tie to the accounts (incurred within 5%) and any history change explained or immaterial; neither holds. Why not stronger than moderate: the history change is small (1.8% of the diagonal, 3.4% of opening reserves), the table's balance to pay ties exactly to the balance sheet, the own-cell incurred miss is only 6.3%, and the incurred test is blunt here (basis-adjusted control -8.1%). If the analysis keeps the record it should use the table's own two diagonals (+118.2m) and flag the sensitivity to the 2016 base (+167.7m); the author should decide. Same age-dependent drift appears (smaller) from the 2015 report to the 2016 table (end-2015 cells 1.023, 1.034, 1.045, 1.070, 1.107 times the 2015 latest), where the US dollar rose against sterling (FX ceiling far larger), so that year is consistent with FX.
